title: Bounded automatic fault retries with a recovery dwell

provenance.adaptation: Independently specified for this project; no public task was copied. The coding assistant chose the state variables, priority order and fixed scan traces, then reviewed the traces against a separate Python transition implementation.
provenance.rationale: A laboratory feeder allows two automatic retries after a transient process fault and locks out a repeatedly failing actuator.
provenance.review: Assistant consistency review of initialization, simultaneous commands, retained state and recovery boundaries; independent Python oracle checked against manual expected traces. Not an industrial safety certification or external expert review.

requirements: States are IDLE, RUNNING, WAIT and LOCKED, initially IDLE with Attempts=0. Start in IDLE starts only when Fault FALSE. A Fault while RUNNING immediately switches off Run. If Attempts<2 enter WAIT, else enter LOCKED. WAIT requires two consecutive Fault=FALSE scans before automatically restarting; a TRUE Fault clears the recovery dwell. Each automatic restart increments Attempts once. LOCKED persists despite Start or Stop. A Reset is accepted only when Fault FALSE and Start FALSE; it returns any state to IDLE and clears Attempts. Otherwise Stop aborts a non-locked state to IDLE and clears its dwell, retaining Attempts. Reset acceptance takes priority over Stop. Run is TRUE only in RUNNING and Locked only in LOCKED. Attempts counts automatic restarts, not the initial operator start. No scan may perform more than one transition.
scenario: A laboratory feeder allows two automatic retries after a transient process fault and locks out a repeatedly failing actuator.

scan_semantics: At scan k, sample every input once, read retained pre-state q[k], execute one transition, and observe outputs O[k] at the end of that same scan. Updated state becomes q[k+1]. Reset the instance before each test. Step 0 executes normally; initial conditions describe pre-state, not an extra delayed scan. All timing in this task is explicitly counted in invocations, not wall time.
assumptions: The fault is an educational process input, not a personnel safety function.
Operator stop/start does not restore the automatic retry budget; only accepted Reset does.

ltl.explanation: A present fault cannot command the feeder.
Automatic restart count stays within the budget.
Accepted reset clears history and leaves the feeder stopped.
Lockout requires a safe explicit reset.
Failure after the second retry exhausts the budget.
Only the second consecutive healthy WAIT scan restarts.
A fault during recovery clears progress and prevents restart.
